I grepped the sheaf-cohomology directory and found no other uses of either lemma. In this file both are used only through explicit `rw`, never through `simp`. I did not run Lean. The shadowing claim rests on simp's usual bottom-up rewriting of subterms with `@[simp]` (post) lemmas. The second lemma's own proof starts by rewriting with the first lemma, which supports that reading. Other lemmas, such as the `@[reassoc]` comparison lemmas, are not simp lemmas and I saw no reason to make them so.

findings.problem: This `@[simp]` lemma competes with `explicitPresheafSectionRepresentative_ι`, which is also `@[simp]`. The first lemma's left-hand side, `explicitPresheafSectionRepresentative F U (colimit.ι (F ⋙ sections U) i s)`, is a proper subterm of the second lemma's left-hand side. Simp rewrites inner subterms first, so the inner term becomes `(colimit.ι (F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf ..) i).app (op U) s` before the outer `.map f.op` is examined. The second lemma's pattern then no longer matches, so as a simp lemma it is effectively dead. The file confirms this: the second lemma's own proof begins with `rw [explicitPresheafSectionRepresentative_ι]`, and the later use at lines 340–341 is a manual `rw`, not `simp`. Also, a simp call on the `map f.op (representative ..)` expression ends in the intermediate form `(underlyingPresheafColimit F).map f.op ((colimit.ι D i).app (op U) s)`. That form is not reduced to `(colimit.ι D i).app (op V) (map f.op s)`, so the desired normal form is not reached.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `underlyingPresheafColimit_map_representative_ι` and keep it as a plain lemma used via `rw`. To get the intended normal form from `simp`, add a simp lemma for the post-rewrite shape instead: `(underlyingPresheafColimit F).map f.op ((colimit.ι D i).app (op U) s) = (colimit.ι D i).app (op V) ((F.obj i).obj.map f.op s)`. Here `D = F ⋙ sheafToPresheaf ..`, and this is exactly the naturality computation in the proof's `h`. The existing `underlyingPresheafColimit_map_representative_ι` then follows from `explicitPresheafSectionRepresentative_ι` plus this lemma. Alternatively, keep a single simp lemma for the composite and drop `@[simp]` from the first.
findings.benefit: The simp set is no longer redundant, and `simp` can reduce restricted representatives to the stage-wise normal form that `exists_stage_of_section_restriction_eq` (line 340) currently reaches by manual `rw`. Readers are no longer misled into thinking the composite rule fires.
